svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
DVWA · 3 components · 2 data flows · 2 trust boundaries · 36 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-2 C-04 → External
Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 C-04 → C-01

df-001: reCAPTCHA verification POST with site secret, user response token and client IP (HTTPS) df-001 authentication: Secret key sent in POST body to the siteverify endpoint; evidence: external/recaptcha/recaptchalib.php:14

df-002: Login lookup and setup queries over mysqli using configured DB credentials (MySQL) df-002 authentication: Configured db_user and db_password passed to mysqli_connect; evidence: dvwa/includes/DBMS/MySQL.php:13
Anonymous Internet Attacker → C-03 · DVWA REST API: scenario 1, 2, 3
Authenticated Internet Attacker → C-03 · DVWA REST API: scenario 4, 6
C-01 · MariaDB database: Database account credentials
C-01 · MariaDB database: User login credentials
Fixed HTTPS endpoint that verifies CAPTCHA responses submitted by DVWA.

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE category: filled = findings in that category
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
A1 ①② = scenarios of attacker A1 · A1 at an arrowhead = its attack
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Request data reaches shell commands and SQL
Unchecked user updates grant admin rights
The recipient checks the supplied password.
The caller presents a configured service credential.
Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
Method properties, not proof of a secure implementation.
